# Rust Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: a patterns skill for writing and reviewing Rust the way experienced Rustaceans do. It enforces idiomatic conventions across six areas: ownership and borrowing so the compiler prevents data races (pass references, take ownership only to store or consume, reach for Cow when ownership is conditional), Result and the ? operator for error propagation with thiserror in libraries and anyhow in applications, enums plus exhaustive pattern matching to make illegal states unrepresentable, traits and generics for zero-cost abstraction, safe concurrency through Arc<Mutex<T>>, channels, and async/await, and small, domain-organized pub surfaces. Every rule ships with good/bad code pairs, so you see the borrow checker friendly version next to the wasteful clone. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; assumes you already know Rust basics, it will not teach the language from zero; examples target modern Rust, very old codebases may diverge. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
